subject: Re: Clarifying 'Availability' and Maintenance Triggers — Olive Analytics MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Olive MSA redlines — availability definition & maintenance triggers

Team,

Samir at Olive sent back their redlines on the MSA/order form earlier today (attached). Two items stand out and I want our legal + ops position before I respond:

1) Availability definition — they want uptime measured as "successful token responses / attempted token responses" at the customer route level and to exclude any traffic routed to fallbacks. They also proposed a 99.7% monthly target for the managed model tier and 99.4% for burst instances.

2) Maintenance window and scheduled updates — they want a 48-hour advance notice for any maintenance that could affect latency or KV cache behavior and are requesting no scheduled maintenance during their business hours 09:00–18:00 ET Mon–Fri. They also propose a formula to prorate service credits based on tokens affected per minute.

Attachments: Olive_MSA_redlines_20280612.docx, SLA_comparison_table_olive_redwood.xlsx

Ask: Laura/legal — can you review the availability metric ask and the proposed credit formula and suggest which redlines we accept, counter, or reject? Karthik — ops needs to quantify if a 48-hour notice plus strict blackout window is operationally feasible and what SLA tiers we can guarantee per region. Hannah — please confirm whether these changes would require a change to our dedicated capacity scheduling calendar and any migration mitigation language.

I'd like to get a consolidated response to Samir by EOD Thursday 6/14.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@olive-analytics.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com

Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:15:22 -0400
Subject: Re: Olive MSA redlines — availability definition & maintenance triggers

Diego,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Apologies for the late hour on our side — our legal team attached the annotated MSA (attached) and a short note on the credit calculation. High level: Olive needs clarity on what "availability" means at the customer route level (we run core payment flows and cannot tolerate transient degradations), and we want maintenance windows to be predictable so we can schedule internal tests.

Requested changes we prefer:
- Explicit exclusion of automatic fallback routing from availability denominator only if the fallback is initiated by Redwood for a documented capacity event.
- A 99.7% monthly uptime guarantee for the Managed tier and 99.5% for Dedicated (we've proposed slightly higher for Dedicated given the reserved capacity).
- Maintenance blackout of major business hours (we listed 09:00–18:00 ET) and a minimum 48-hour advance notification for any planned maintenance that could change the API surface or KV cache semantics.
- Service credit formula: prorated by minutes of degraded service and weight by percent of successful responses lost, with a cap equal to one month of fees per incident.

We are open to discussion but need to lock down a language that prevents surprise degradations during our peak window.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Ops, Olive Analytics
---
Attachments: Olive_MSA_redlines_20280612.docx (annotated)

From: laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 11:42:08 -0700
Subject: RE: Olive MSA redlines — availability definition & maintenance triggers

Diego — I reviewed the annotated MSA and populated the attached comparison matrix with our recommended positions. Summary of suggested responses:

- Availability metric: counterproposal to measure availability as "successful request responses / total requests accepted by our ingress layer", with explicit note that automated fallbacks initiated by Redwood for capacity degradation are excluded only when routed by our system as a configured fallback policy. This mirrors our policy for other enterprise customers and avoids the denominator manipulation risk.

- Uptime targets: propose 99.6% monthly for Managed, 99.5% for Dedicated (we_can_accept_higher_reserved_commitments), with a 3-tier credit schedule rather than per-minute prorating. Reason: per-minute weighting is operationally noisy and hard to audit.

- Maintenance notice: we can commit to 48-hour windows for non-critical updates. For kernel / runtime patches that require immediate remediation, we need an exception with post-notification and a defined postmortem SLA. Suggest adding language that we will not schedule non-emergency maintenance during their specified blackout window without written consent.

- Credits cap: accept a per-incident cap equal to monthly fees, not to exceed three months per rolling 12-month period.

I'll attach the matrix and a redline snippet for the availability paragraph. If Karthik confirms ops feasibility on the blackout window, I recommend we propose the above and push back on the per-minute prorating.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: Redwood_Position_matrix_olive_20280613.xlsx, availability_paragraph_redline.txt

From: karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com <karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com, diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 16:26:51 -0700
Subject: RE: Olive MSA redlines — availability definition & maintenance triggers

Quick ops readout:

- 48-hour advance notice for planned maintenance is fine for control-plane updates and scheduled kernel rollouts. We cannot guarantee zero maintenance during 09:00–18:00 ET across all regions — there are cross-region dependencies and occasional security patches that need coordinated windows. That said, we can offer a mitigation: reserve up to two ad-hoc emergency maintenance windows per 12 months that may fall within their blackout window with immediate post-notification and a 48-hour follow-up report.

- Regarding the proposed per-minute token weighting: we will not be able to produce a precise per-minute token impact metric in real time without adding instrumentation that will increase cost. We can, however, agree to a time-bucketed approach (5–15 minute buckets) and provide post-incident sampling that demonstrates percent impact.

- Dedicated capacity: we can commit to a higher baseline (99.5–99.6) depending on reserved GPU count & pinned model versions. Need Diego to confirm their desired Dedicated commit if Olive wants higher SLA.

Karthik
VP, Production Engineering

From: hannah.schmitt@redwood-inference.com <hannah.schmitt@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: RE: Olive MSA redlines — availability definition & maintenance triggers

Agree with Laura and Karthik. Quick operational asks before we send our consolidated reply to Olive:

1) Diego — can you confirm whether Olive plans to move core flows to Dedicated or stay Managed for the first 6 months? That materially changes the SLA we should propose.
2) Laura — can you prepare the redline snippet that explicitly describes the "fallback exclusion" criteria (i.e., must be a documented, automated fallback triggered by our capacity policy) and a short audit clause for how we will provide evidence for the credit calculation?
3) Karthik — please add wording for the emergency maintenance carveout (two ad-hoc events / 12 months, post-notification and postmortem within 72 hours).

If we can get those three items in the next 12 hours I'll send the consolidated reply to Samir and copy legal for final signoff.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
